purpose: Vonoprazan is used to treat heartburn and damage to the esophagus caused by acid reflux, a condition called erosive esophagitis. It is also used along with antibiotics to get rid of a stomach bacteria called H. pylori. It helps your stomach make less acid so you feel better and your body can heal.
how_it_works: Your stomach has tiny pumps that release acid to help digest food, but sometimes too much acid causes problems. Vonoprazan works by blocking a key part of those pumps called the potassium channel, which stops them from releasing acid. Unlike older acid-reducing medicines, it works quickly and keeps acid under control for a longer period of time.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include stomach pain, nausea, diarrhea, and gas. Some people may also notice headache or an upset stomach. These side effects are usually mild and tend to go away as your body gets used to the medicine.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, as this medicine may need to be used with caution. Long-term use of acid-blocking medicines can sometimes lower magnesium levels or affect how your body absorbs certain vitamins like B12. This medicine may interact with other drugs, so always tell your pharmacist and doctor about everything you take, including supplements. Seek medical attention right away if you develop severe diarrhea, as it could be a sign of a serious infection.
typical_dosing: For erosive esophagitis, the usual dose is 20 mg taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. For H. pylori treatment, it is typically taken twice a day along with antibiotics for 2 weeks. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your situation.
